_cronsReference.name: Follow_Ups
_cronsReference.description: Check non-responsive leads every 7 min; send_followups itself only sends inside CONTACT_WINDOWS (12:33-13:57 and 16:03-18:30 CAT), so off-hours ticks are no-ops. Each lead fires at its own jittered minute for natural human send times. Formerly named superb-tenderness.

_cronsReference.name: Reminders
_cronsReference.description: Customer and plumber reminders - booking, morning, 2hr, 30min alerts.

_cronsReference.name: Email_Follow_Ups
_cronsReference.command: PLUMBOT_CRON=send_scheduled_followups,process_inbound_emails,send_job_reminders,summarize_unconfirmed_leads   [TO ADD, in this order and only after verifying each with --dry-run: send_post_visit_followups (backlog-guarded, ready), then send_plan_quote_followups, send_phone_quote_followups, send_visit_checkins -- all four commands have shipped]
_cronsReference.description: Carries every job that is not the main follow-up or reminder cron: staff-queued ScheduledFollowup dispatch over WhatsApp or email (including email follow-ups for delayed leads), IMAP inbound-email polling, job reminders, 24h unconfirmed-lead summaries, and the post-visit machine (the 35-minute debrief-form email to the plumber, the Case A/B/C quote follow-ups to the lead, and the cold handback). Also the plan path (send_plan_quote_followups): a lead who sends a real plan needs no site visit, so the plumber is emailed the job plus the plan an hour after it arrives (or as soon as the description, area and timeline are in), chased at +2h/+4h/+8h until they answer the one-tap form, and the lead is asked about the quote an hour after the plumber confirms or at +12h assuming it went out. ORDER MATTERS: add a job to PLUMBOT_CRON only AFTER the deploy that ships its command. start.sh keeps going past a failing job but exits 1 at the end, so an unknown command marks the WHOLE service Crashed on every tick — and a service that is always red is one where a real failure goes unnoticed. This was done the wrong way round on 2026-09-06 (variable set at 01:45, code not deployed) and every 5-minute run showed Crashed until it was rolled back. SAFE TO ENABLE NOW: send_post_visit_followups is still absent from the live PLUMBOT_CRON and the whole post-visit machine has therefore never run. The backlog that blocked it is now handled IN CODE by POST_VISIT_BACKLOG_DAYS (default 3, see bot/post_visit.py): a finished visit with no report yet is left alone once it is that stale, so switching the job on picks up only the last few days instead of firing ~25 emails about visits going back months. The guard gates OPENING a report and never ticking one that exists, so nothing already in flight is stranded. Verify first with `python manage.py send_post_visit_followups --dry-run` and read the counters -- `stale=` is what the guard declined, everything else is what the next real tick would send; the dry run creates nothing, deliberately, because a dry run that created report rows would arm the very backlog it was meant to preview. THEN add send_post_visit_followups to PLUMBOT_CRON on the Email_Follow_Ups service (the command has shipped since 2026-09, so the deploy-order trap below does not apply to it). And the future-dated visit check-ins (send_visit_checkins): a lead who wants the job in a month is penciled in for a real day near their target, then asked to confirm it by email at target minus 7 and minus 4 days, with a yes and a no link; a lead with no email has those two go to the plumber instead, carrying a prefilled WhatsApp message they can send from their own phone. All seven are idempotent - every send is gated by a timestamp written as it goes out - so a 5-minute tick re-running them is safe. Formerly named delightful-eagerness.

_cronsReference.name: Plumbot_v1
_cronsReference.description: The gunicorn web service. PLUMBOT_CRON must stay unset here or start.sh would run a cron job instead of booting the site.

_note: This file applies to EVERY service in the project and its startCommand overrides each service's own. Cron services therefore share start.sh and pick their job(s) via the PLUMBOT_CRON env var (comma-separated for several jobs per tick). The list above is documentation only - Railway does not read it.
_cronScheduleTrap: A Railway deployment BAKES IN the cron schedule that the service had at the moment the deployment was created. A deployment built while the schedule was absent comes out buildOnly=false with cronSchedule=null: it runs start.sh once at deploy time and then NEVER ticks again, even though the service page still shows a schedule and Railway keeps advancing nextCronRunAt. That is silent - the deployment sits at SUCCESS with no error anywhere. It killed send_followups from 2026-08-25 01:53 UTC until 2026-08-28 12:26 UTC; the only follow-ups that went out in that time were the ones a human triggered with the dashboard's manual follow-up check button, which runs the command inside the WEB service. `railway redeploy` does NOT fix it - it replays the bad snapshot. Re-apply the schedule to the service (serviceInstanceUpdate cronSchedule) and then deploy fresh (serviceInstanceDeployV2). To verify a cron service is genuinely live, check its latest deployment meta: buildOnly must be true and serviceManifest.deploy.cronSchedule must hold the schedule, and its deploymentLogs must show a '[start.sh] cron job' line per tick.
